findings.title: No automated tests found
findings.evidence: 49 source files and 0 test files (searched tests/, __tests__/, test_*.py, *_test.py, *.test.*, *.spec.*).
findings.explanation: Without tests there is no fast, repeatable way to know whether a change breaks existing behaviour.
findings.impact: Regressions reach users; refactoring (including fixes from this report) is risky.
findings.remediation: Start with tests for the most critical paths (auth, payments, data writes), using pytest/Vitest.

findings.title: `classify` has cyclomatic complexity 55
findings.explanation: Cyclomatic complexity counts independent paths (branches, loops, boolean operators, handlers). 55 exceeds the threshold of 15. The number is exact; the threshold is a convention.
findings.impact: Each path needs a test to be covered; complex functions hide edge-case bugs and are risky to change.
findings.remediation: Extract branches into well-named helpers, use early returns, or replace conditionals with lookup tables/polymorphism.

findings.title: Bare `except:` catches everything
findings.explanation: A bare except also catches KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, and hides programming errors such as NameError.
findings.impact: Failures are silently converted into wrong behaviour; shutdown can be blocked.
findings.remediation: Catch the specific exceptions you expect (e.g. `except ValueError:`).

findings.title: Exception is caught and ignored
findings.explanation: The handler body only contains `pass`/`continue`, so the error is discarded without logging or recovery.
findings.impact: Bugs and outages become invisible; data may be left half-written.
findings.remediation: Log the error with context, re-raise, or handle it explicitly.

findings.title: Empty catch block
findings.explanation: The catch block has no statements, so the error is silently discarded.
findings.impact: Failures become invisible and debugging becomes guesswork.
findings.remediation: Log the error, rethrow it, or handle it explicitly; add a comment if ignoring is truly intended.

findings.title: Circular dependency between 2 modules
findings.explanation: These modules import each other (directly or transitively). The import path shown was resolved from the source; it is not a guess.
findings.impact: Cycles make modules impossible to understand, test or reuse in isolation, can cause partially-initialised imports at runtime (Python) or undefined values (ES modules), and block clean layering.
findings.remediation: Extract the shared code into a lower-level module that both depend on, or invert one dependency (pass a callback/interface instead of importing).

findings.title: `process` is 203 lines long
findings.explanation: Functions over 80 lines usually do more than one thing.
findings.impact: Long functions are hard to read, review and test in isolation.
findings.remediation: Split into smaller functions that each do one named step.

findings.title: Class `GodObject` has 33 methods across 131 lines
findings.explanation: Very large classes frequently mix several responsibilities (a 'god class'). This is inferred from size alone; review whether the methods share one purpose.
findings.impact: Changes for unrelated reasons collide in one class; testing requires heavy setup.
findings.remediation: Identify clusters of methods that use the same fields and extract them.
